old_title: Australia 42-38 South Africa: international men's rugby union Test - live reaction
new_title: Australia 42-38 South Africa: international men's rugby union Test - as it happened
old_text:
"Simply couldn't have come at a better time for the Wallabies and Rugby Australia," emails Marlon Maton. "Big ticket release for the World Cup coming up. That's just massive."
All of which occurred after Erasmus had emptied his entire interchange at the start of the second half - only to find the cupboard bare when he needed to withdraw the injured Etzebeth, and with the referee communicating to his TMO via a mobile phone after the radio communications repeatedly failed. Pure chaos.
The Wallabies were cruising at 42-17 with just 15 minutes remaining, coasting towards a statement victory over a weakened South African side, then the final quarter of an hour saw four yellow cards and the Springboks reduce the margin to just four points by the final whistle.
CONVERTED TRY! Australia 42-38 South Africa (Nche, 80)
Australia overthrow the 10m lineout but South Africa can't capitalise. The Wallabies regroup, milk the clock but then turn the ball over with one-out drives! The Sptingboks pour forward, surely they score this time - but it's disjointed and they have to return to the penalty advantage. Marx taps and goes. He's held up. Just seconds left. Nche! Yes! Is there time for the conversion? Yes! Is there time for the restart? Who knows!?
78 mins: South Africa kick to the right on the 22 and look certain to score on the left wing but Jorgensen makes a majestic tackle. Then the Springboks seem destined to score on the right edge through Marx but the defence is desperate and Wright toe pokes the ball clear!
76 mins: I see it, but I don't believe it. The 12 man Wallabies have just sealed the most preposterous victory! South Africa take the restart on the 22 then the 15 set about the 12 along the left touchline. Play comes infield towards the acres of empty space - but Tom Wright reads it like a book, places himself in the road, intercepts, and canters over to send the crowd into delirium! Wow!
CONVERTED TRY! Australia 42-31 South Africa (van den Berg, 74)
The scrum holds, van den Berg picks up the pieces and crashes over next to the left upright. The conversion is unmissable and we have six minutes of mayhem to go!
73 mins: Piardi is talking to the two skippers, trying to calm things down, figuring out how Australia can pack a scrum with just 12 men. Play will restart with the Springboks packing down 5m from the line.
72 mins: IT IS ON! South Africa hammer downfield from the restart, carving through the undermanned defence. They reach the left corner in no time, then kick crossfield for van der Merwe to collect and touchdown - but he knocks on! Massive let-off for Australia - but hang on...
The scrum is unstoppable, the try is inevitable, but Australia try to spoil it on the line with Lonergan miles offside. That is as clear a penalty try as you could design... and...
70 mins: Finally the scrum is fed. South Africa get the shove on, and they appear to be over the line, but Piardi is on the blindside so he has to call on his TMO for eyes in the sky. Replays show a knock-on over the line so play is called back for an earlier penalty.
The past couple of minutes of game time have taken about 15 minutes of actual time. Sometimes rugby is its own worst enemy. Piardi is back on the blower. Deary me this is a shemozzle.
After review, Australia's skipper has been sent to the bin for his part coming second man in and dropping his shoulder into the falling Marx. The Wallabies will have to defend with just 14 for the final ten minutes.
69 mins: Play resumes with Feinberg-Mngomezulu kicking to the right corner. Of course it's then Etzebeth who accepts the lineout throw and sets up the maul. It's destined for the right corner but Australia do well to hold it up. The ball comes out and two runners hit the line at searing pace - the second of whom, Marx - is clotheslined by Suaalii and finished off by Wilson's shoulder. 5m scrum penalty under the posts.
68 mins: There's a delay while officials figure out what to do with Etzebeth. South Africa have emptied their bench but the big lock forward doesn't look right. The Springboks seem to be trying to lobby for a head injury replacement.
68 mins: South Africa are stung. They up the intensity as they go through phases on the right but when they come infield Suaalii is quick at the breakdown. Play is called back to an earlier advantage near halfway. "Working Class Man" by Jimmy Barnes blares through the PA system, presumably ironically.
What is happening out there!? South Africa are imploding! For the third passage in succession a straightforward attacking play ends in calamity. This time it's disjointed in midfield, Moodie spills a mistimed pass, and Jorgensen is first to the loose ball. He scoops up the loose pill, and hares off at warp speed, covering the 60m to the right corner in a flash, much to the delight and disbelief of the Optus Stadium crowd. This is staggering.
64 mins: Better lineout from the Springboks this time, looping the ball long out the back and the support runners hit the 22 - but then de Jager spills in contact! Who is this team in green, and what have they done with South Africa?
62 mins: For the second time tonight a South African restart has Australia in all sorts but Wright scrambles well and the ball is cleared to the 22 - where the Springbok lineout is spoiled and a gold jersey gathers the shrapnel on the deck. This has been an uncharacteristic half from the World Cup holders.
CONVERTED TRY! Australia 37-17 South Africa (Wilson, 60)
Wilson will not be denied twice! The 5m tap and go penalty sets up another passage of manic pick-and-go grunt and shunt work and this time Wilson is too quick and strong for the South African defence.
58 mins: The set-piece holds allowing Suaalii to hit the line at speed off the back. Inches from the line it's frenzied pick and go. There's an offside penalty advantage on the play. Gold and green jerseys mass around the line like eels wriggling in a rock pool. Can Australia find the out ball again? Yes! It's Wilson on the left wing and he spins and rolls over in the corner! But did he creep into touch? Just! Agonising for the Wallaby skipper but play returns to the penalty advantage.
57 mins: Lonergan feeds the scrum 30m out then invites Paisami nto the line. Wilson has a smash, then it's out to the backs for Wright to bring Potter into the fray on the left touchline. He's hauled down just 5m from home so it's back to the big lads. Tupou inches closer, Salakaia-Loto throws his weight around, the left corner looks inevitable - but then the whistle blows and there's a knock-on... against green! Australia with the 5m scrum.
55 mins: Ikitau has succumbed to his pain so Potter comes on and Suaalii will shift into the centres. From the restart Australia are secure, control play for a few phases then Lonergan launches another towering box kick that Lonergan steams onto like a border collie catching a frisbee at the beach. That skill is becoming a serious weapon for the Wallabies. Play moves from right to left and scrambling on the back foot the Springboks concede their latest breakdown penalty. The No 1 side in the world are being seriously tested here. And they won't want to see Etzebeth chugging painkillers with the bench already emptied.
52 mins: More scrappy play from both sides that ends with a South Africa knock-on, then Etzebeth is penalised for an incorrect clearout. Things not going the Springboks' way at the moment. Meanwhile Ikitau doesn't look great, limping away from the physio after heavy contact on the ground.
49 mins: This is as controlled and disciplined Australia have played against a top tier nation in a long time. And the good times continue with Jorgensen winning the clearing box kick from the restart. The Wallabies go through hands from right to left but Suaalii is stopped in his tracks and possession is kicked away. The Springboks enjoy some slow phase play on halfway before van den berg hoists a garryowen that comes down in green hands. With the home defence backtracking there's space in behind for a kick to the left corner and a chance to execute a squeeze.
46 mins: Not for long though with a spilled carry and a couple of kicks ahead earning the Wallabies some ugly metres. Etzebeth tries to establish some order in his red zone but the clearing kick only reaches the 22. Australia can't get any fluidity in their attack but South Africa are too desperate in defence with a hand in the ruck inviting Lonergan an opportunity to extend the lead.
44 mins: Williams steals the lineout! What a couple of minutes from the big second rower. Australia attack from left to right but it's all very flat. Then they reverse direction and Suaalii gets too cute with his no-look pass and the ball is knocked on. Both teams try to counter in broken field as structure goes out of the window. For South Africa it's Hooker tearing down the left wing, but he runs into Wilson, gets stopped in his tracks and Australia can settle things down.
42 mins: South Africa get the first opportunity of the half with Suaalii penalised on halfway allowing the Springboks to kick to the 22. But the lineout doesn't go anywhere and Williams wins a massive turnover penalty. That was a big win for the Australian pack.
CONVERTED TRY! Australia 24-17 South Africa (Donaldson, 39)
The lineout is contested but it comes down gold. Australia go through hands from left to right then Wright dabs a Messi-like through-ball to Jorgensen on the right touchline. The winger just remains infield and with momentum almost crosses the try-line. The Wallabies recycle infield then get into some serious grind, going to-to-toe with the Springboks one-out. 14 phases - then they strike! Lonergan is quick at the ruck, then it's crisp catch and pass with precise execution to allow Suaalii to offload to Donaldson on his outside and cruise over in the left corner. That is the second magnificent try of the half from the hosts that demonstrates patience in sight of a score, decision making, and execution to go with it.
37 mins: Now there's a delay while the TMO takes a look at something. It's a clash of heads between Hooker on Donaldson as the Australian took possession of a high ball. The tackle is fierce - and legal to begin with - but then there's head-on-head contact so a penalty to the Wallabies; nothing more.
37 mins: Australia go from 22 to 22 from the scrum with Ikitau bursting downfield. He's hunted down by green jerseys allowing the Wallabies to go through the phases with attacking territory but yet again it's poor connection in midfield and the ball is knocked on. The Springboks respond by kicking behind and chasing hard, winning the ball back on the ground. Fassie senses chaos equals opportunity and dashes on the outside down the left, kicks ahead but Jorgensen is well placed and claims the mark. Breathless stuff. Brilliant running rugby from Ikitau and Fassie, superb collective defensive from the Springboks, excellent scrambling from the hosts.
35 mins: From the resulting scrum, 30m out, there's room to the left but Fassi can't pull in a pass that's a fraction behind him. Ikitau's eyes light up at the possibility of a 70m counter but he fumbles the loose ball.
33 mins: South Africa kick to halfway after Alaalatoa is penalised for head-to-head contact in the tackle. The Springboks mount a scruffy attack that is resisted powerfully by Valetini. Bell then looks to have secured clean turnover ball, only to spill it forward after doing all the hard work.
CONVERTED TRY! Australia 17-17 South Africa (Van der Merwe, 30)
It's a shootout in Perth! South Africa secure turnover ball on halfway, create a maul, and from a penalty advantage launch two beautiful passes out to the right, first from Pollard, then Moodie, splitting the Australian defence apart, then it's textbook timing catch and pass to allow Van der Merwe to show his pace and streak into the corner.
Pollard is as consistent as Lonergan and we're tied once more.
CONVERTED TRY! Australia 17-10 South Africa (Ikitau, 28)
Ikitau has two in the blink of an eye! The Wallabies scrum holds and there's a break down the right. With penalty advantage Bell and Wilson hit the line hard allowing Lonergan time to pick his spot with his boot - and that spot is 15m in front of the charging Suaalii - who leaps, spoils Fassi in the air - and Ikitau is front and square to pick up the crumbs and scamper over the line. That was very rugby league areas from the former Rooster, and also AFL at the home of the Eagles and Dockers, with the big forward bringing the ball to ground for the little fella to do his work.
26 mins: A bunch of Boks are offside from the restart so we'll have a scrum on halfway. A chance to praise Wilson for his decision to go for the try instead of the penalty a few moments ago. It has become a feature of his captaincy.

I will be back here for the next chapter in the Bledisloe Cup rivalry, but for now I shall leave you with Angus Fontaine, Jack Snape and their thoughts from the final whistle in Perth.
If that unbeaten run is to extend to seven matches the Wallabies will have to overcome the greatest of all rugby's challenges: the All Blacks at Eden Park. That is a week on Saturday.
The first words Les Kiss tells the host broadcaster are words of praise for his coaching staff for keeping everyone calm. Then he moves on to hoping the fallout from the match focuses on the first 60 minutes, when Australia were dominant, than the crazy final 15 when mayhem ruled.
The selection of Suaalii on the wing was the main talking point before kick-off, and it paid dividends for Les Kiss. Time and again Lonergan and Wright went to the skies for the the No 11 and his wing partner Jorgensen to collect mid-air like magnetic wrecking balls. The Springboks had no answer, and not only does it give the Wallabies a serious weapon, it has a knock on effect in open play with South Africa reluctant to engage in kicking exchanges for fear of being monstered overhead.
The stats back it up with Australia approaching 600 kick metres, South Africa just over 300.
As Harry Wilson accepts the Nelson Mandela Plate, is it too soon to ask if the Wallabies are back? They've been away a while, and plumbed some depths, but the pack held its own against the very best, the backs were effervescent, the set-piece was solid, the kicking game was smart... and if they could find a No 10 they might even become contenders.
